merger_description:
The Altius Group (**Altius**), via its wholly owned subsidiary, Altius Bidco Pty Ltd, proposes to acquire 100% of the issued share capital of Converge International Pty Ltd (**Converge**) (the **Acquisition**).

Altius is a workplace health and wellbeing service provider owned by a fund managed by Riverside Company, a private equity firm. Its services include:

* Occupational rehabilitation and injury management services to support physically or psychologically injured workers return to work.
* Workplace health, wellbeing and employee support services. This includes both general services (such as workplace  and safety services and executive health assessments) and psychological services. Psychological services include both ‘preventative’ services (such as organisational psychology and employee counselling), and ‘treatment’ services to support employees in distress (such as employee assistance program (**EAP**) offerings and critical incident response (**CIR**) services).
* Ancillary services such as psychometric assessments, training and consulting.

Converge is an Australian EAP and workplace wellbeing service provider. Its core business is focused on providing EAP/CIR services, while also offering various other workplace health, wellbeing and employee support services. Similar to Altius, Converge also offers ancillary services such as psychometric assessments, training and consulting.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The aggregation in the supply of EAP and critical incident
response services resulting from the Acquisition is estimated to
be low.
• The aggregation in the supply of the relevant ancillary employee
psychology and workplace wellness services resulting from the
Acquisition is also estimated to be low.
• Post-Acquisition, the merged entity would continue to face
competition from multiple alternative suppliers of EAP and
critical incident response services, as well as multiple alternative
suppliers of the relevant ancillary employee psychology and
workplace wellness services.
